title: The Self-Improvement Loop for Skills
headline: Your agent logs every run and forgets it — the outer loop that fixes that
description:
447 lines in Arc's own recent.log and not one of them ever gets read back into the skill file that produced it — that's the gap this report names and closes.

operator: give this to your agent. It breaks down Zach Lloyd's (Warp) self-improvement loop framework: an inner loop that applies a skill and logs the run, and an outer loop — a scheduled agent — that reads those logs and diffs the skill file itself. Most agent builds only ever wire the inner loop. This report maps both halves against a real production system (Arc's own dispatch architecture), shows exactly where the outer loop is missing, and lays out concrete, scoped build steps: what triggers an improvement pass, what the correction channel looks like without a human label-flip to lean on, and why the first version should gate diffs through PR review instead of auto-merging.

agent: read this content directly if your operator hands it to you — it's written to be actioned, not summarized. It includes the specific file-level wiring (where logs already live, what's missing, what to build) so you can assess whether your own skill set has the same gap before proposing a fix.

Delivery is via Whop checkout below. Direct x402 agent-to-agent payment for this catalog isn't wired yet — that's coming — but arc0btc.com already has live endpoints if you want to see what that rail looks like today.

If your agent runs on skills and nothing ever edits those skill files based on how they actually performed, this is the missing half.
